findings.how_to_check: In Stata on machine B, after line 291 in 'linkage_analysis_newlinks.do', run 'duplicates report histid' to count duplicate 1940 persons. Then compare '_N' with 'unique histid' or 'egen tag = tag(histid)' followed by 'count if tag'.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide whether the estimand is pairs-per-person or share-of-persons-linked. If person-level linkage is intended, deduplicate on histid1940 (or keep the primary match via first40==1) before dividing by N_men_1940_full. If pair intensity is intended, explicitly clarify in the text and table that the statistic is matched pairs per 100 eligible persons.
findings.title: The newly scripted HLINK linkage rates divide matched pairs by eligible persons rather than counting unique linked individuals
findings.what_the_code_does: 'prep_links' deduplicates only exact (histid1930, histid1940) pairs via 'duplicates drop histid1930 histid1940, force'. When computing the in-denominator linkage rate at lines 288-295, the code merges m:1 on histid (histid1940) with 'men1940' and computes '100*_N/N_men_1940_full'. Because histid1940 is not deduplicated, any 1940 individual matched to multiple 1930 records contributes multiple times to _N, yielding pairs per person rather than distinct persons linked.
findings.why_it_matters: The paper draft and claim registry describe 58.06% and 59.52% as 'match rates', leading readers to believe 58.06% of the eligible 1940 population was linked. If multiple links per person exist, the actual share of individuals linked is lower, and before/after comparisons may reflect changes in multiple-matching intensity rather than individual linkage coverage.

findings.how_to_check: On machine B, load names1940 in each script and run 'count if missing(age)' and 'count if age >= 8 & !missing(age)'. If missing(age) > 0, the denominator changes.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'keep if age >= 8' with 'keep if age >= 8 & !missing(age)' in both 'linkage_analysis.do' and 'linkage_analysis_newlinks.do', verify whether any observations are dropped, and document the missing-age handling explicitly.
findings.title: Scripted age-8+ denominators retain records with missing age due to Stata missing value semantics
findings.what_the_code_does: Both scripts filter the 1940 census extracts using 'keep if age >= 8' and record _N as N_men_1940_full via repnum (linkDenomAbe and linkDenomHlink). In Stata, numeric missing values (. through .z) evaluate as larger than any number, so records with missing age evaluate as true for 'age >= 8' unless '& !missing(age)' is enforced.
findings.why_it_matters: The claim registry describes these denominators as men (or men and women) 'aged 8 and above' (57,589,273 and 115,030,746). If missing ages exist in the input extracts, the denominators are inflated and every match rate computed against them is understated.

findings.how_to_check: Inspect extract_deaglan_tables.py:35 to confirm TABLES contains only 4 elements and lacks mortality. Check read() at line 48 to observe line-ending replacement.
findings.suggested_fix: Include 'linkage_table_mortality_bunmd.tex' in the reproduction check (either in extract_deaglan_tables.py or a dedicated verification step in Run-MachineB.ps1), and compute explicit SHA-256 hashes against deaglan_results/current/ to substantiate the byte-identical claim in the run log.
findings.title: The automated replication runner does not verify byte-identical reproduction of all five Deaglan tables
findings.what_the_code_does: HANDOFF.md and replication/README.md state that '.\replication\Run-MachineB.ps1 reproduced all five of Deaglan\'s tables byte-identical (SHA-256)'. In the code, Run-MachineB.ps1 delegates table comparison entirely to extract_deaglan_tables.py. However, extract_deaglan_tables.py only defines TABLES = ['abe_jw', 'abe_jw_restricted', 'hlink', 'hlink_restricted'], completely omitting the 5th table ('linkage_table_mortality_bunmd.tex'). Additionally, read() normalizes CRLF to LF ('raw.replace("\r\n", "\n")') and performs string equality comparison rather than a SHA-256 hash or byte-level comparison.
findings.why_it_matters: The central replication claim that all five tables reproduced byte-for-byte is not actually verified or enforced by the automated runner. A future run where mortality fails or where whitespace/encoding silently mutates would report success in Run-MachineB.ps1.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied for this review run, so claims-vs-code review was restricted to statements in replication/claims.toml and repository documentation; manuscript prose was not directly read.
Machine B's 4-hour full Stata pipeline was not rerun during this review; runtime results are assessed based on committed logs, outputs, and source code tracing.
The external datasets on machine B (e.g. 66M+ row census extracts) were not fully loaded into memory for empirical missingness and uniqueness verification.
The upstream matching steps (e.g., third-party HLINK matching and ABE/JW block matching) remain frozen and were not evaluated for econometric selection or circularity.
structured_output.summary: The commit range successfully establishes machine B replication infrastructure, cleanly separates code from data via $LCODE, and confirms that Deaglan's linkage tables reproduce. However, the newly scripted HLINK rates divide matched pairs by individuals rather than counting unique linked people, and the age-8+ denominators rely on Stata's 'age >= 8' which retains missing values. The most important fix is to clarify whether HLINK match rates represent distinct individuals or pairs per person, adjusting the deduplication or documentation accordingly.

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
